headline: High-risk workspace overlap: both agents can write shared code and secrets-bearing contexts, creating dangerous conflict and leakage pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can use MCP, browsers, and shared integrations, while Replit Agent reads/writes Repl workspace files. A shared filesystem or copied artifacts could let attacker-controlled content in one agent’s outputs influence the other, but no direct default bridge is documented here. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange files through a shared workspace or copied artifacts, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF either agent treats file contents as instructions without provenance checks, the risk materializes.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of peer-generated files.
Add a provenance banner to all exchanged artifacts.
Require manual review before executing instructions from files.
Use separate directories for each agent.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filtering in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, and docs, and Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration. If they share a workspace or copied artifacts, sensitive material can flow between them; the profiles do not prove isolation, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF both agents access the same repository or workspace files, leakage of secrets or internal docs is possible.
IF either agent uploads file contents to its backend during analysis, copied sensitive data can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces and repos per agent.
Remove secrets from any shared files before handoff.
Use redacted exports for cross-agent review.
Rotate any credentials exposed in shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls and secret scanning.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, modify git state, read/write filesystems, and use broad network egress. Devin also has shared-state integrations, while Replit Agent’s Repl filesystem persists across sessions. Concurrent writes to the same repo or mutable resources can cause irreversible git or deployment conflicts by default if paired.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git branch or workspace, write conflicts are likely.
IF either agent pushes or deploys without locking, one agent can overwrite the other’s changes.
mitigations: Assign separate branches per agent.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use lock files for shared mutable resources.
Require human approval before git push or deploy.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is a long-running planner-executor and Replit Agent is a single planner agent with tool calls; both can act autonomously on code and deployment tasks. If one agent’s output is handed to the other as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect code or deployment actions. The profiles do not show a verification gate, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF one agent’s generated plan or code is forwarded to the other without review, cascading errors can propagate.
IF the second agent is allowed to act on the first agent’s output directly, downstream mistakes can become actions.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require tests before accepting peer output.
Limit the second agent to read-only critique.
Annotate outputs with confidence and provenance.
requires-engineering: add structured verification between planner and executor roles.

E_compliance.rationale: Devin explicitly handles team chat, issue trackers, docs, and integration tokens, while Replit Agent handles secrets and deployment configuration. If regulated or sensitive data is moved between their cloud environments, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF regulated data such as secrets or internal chat content is copied between the two vendors, compliance obligations may differ.
IF one environment retains artifacts longer than the other, deletion and retention requirements can diverge.
mitigations: Avoid moving regulated data between vendors.
Strip secrets from shared artifacts.
Confirm retention settings in both products.
Use separate tenants for sensitive projects.
requires-engineering: obtain vendor DPAs and map residency/retention controls.
